tasks.title: Bound aggregate scan export input and output allocations
evidence: Verified code path: ScanApi::export_many accepts up to 50 IDs and collects all ScanResults before render_many.
MAX_RESULTS_BYTES permits 64 MiB per results file. Theoretical aggregate serialized allowance is 50 x 64 MiB = 3200 MiB before parsing/output overhead; no RSS or OOM was measured.
PipelineLimits.max_export_bytes already defaults to 8 MiB. Existing single/multiple exports create intermediate rows and complete output buffers.
interfaces: Reuse ScanStore::results safety and private atomic storage; add budget-aware reading at the existing bounded I/O boundary before allocation. Avoid a metadata-check/reopen race.
Apply checked cumulative input and output accounting; include JSON escaping, CSV quoting and XLSX container overhead. Validate format and repeated IDs before loading.

Preserve small-output schemas and row order. Reject over-budget work with an explicit existing-compatible error and useful UI message; never silently truncate or report partial output as complete. Streaming is acceptable only where the current response contract and aggregate limits remain enforced.
tasks.done_when: Regression fixtures prove exact-boundary success, one-byte-over refusal before aggregate allocation, checked arithmetic, duplicate-ID policy, escaping expansion and unchanged small SpiderFoot exports. tasks.title: Cap expensive saved-scan operations before worker and body allocation
evidence: Verified code path: web_server::scans_response starts a 4 MiB-stack worker per admitted saved-scan request; the general connection limit is 32.
A distinct admission cap for heavy saved-scan requests is absent at this boundary. Multiplied memory/latency impact is a supported risk, not a measured OOM.
interfaces: Reuse existing atomic/RAII permit patterns; acquire the heavy-operation permit before spawning or loading. Keep quick health/control/stop paths responsive.
Return a bounded 503 response when capacity is exhausted. Release permits on success, error, panic, spawn failure and connection teardown.
Keep current host/origin/token protections, response schemas and Web UI retry semantics. Surface capacity rejection in the existing status UI; no root privileges or Android packet interception.
tasks.done_when: Synchronized requests prove peak admitted heavy work never exceeds the chosen documented cap and permits recover on every exit path. Existing phone-sized browser CI passes, including useful capacity errors and unchanged health/control behavior.

tasks.title: Integrate shared failure suppression without duplicate provider throttlers
evidence: Verified opt-in gap: shared FetchOptions::paced exists; inspected GitHub, HIBP and DeHashed send paths use unpaced no_redirects options.
HIBP/DeHashed already have provider-specific rate limiters. stolen.tax has bounded retries. A second independent limiter could increase delays and request costs.
interfaces: Use the existing shared host breaker where compatible; retain provider-specific Retry-After and one authoritative retry budget.
Treat 429, timeout, challenge/WAF, failed authentication, legitimate empty response and confirmed miss as distinct source outcomes. No failure-to-not-found conversion.
No additional paid requests or retry multiplication. Isolate unrelated hosts and make recovery bounded and observable without logging keys.
